findings.summary: §1.1 read chain is broken at its very first step against the real artifact. The entry extracts the drain summary with `grep -oE '\{[^{}]*"drain_id"[^{}]*\}'`, a brace-free regex. The verbatim real summary (spec §0 GT-1) is `{"reason":"drained","rounds":1,"ticksByLabel":{"tick":1},"runs_root":"…","drain_id":"…"}` — it contains a nested object before drain_id, so no match can start at either `{`: from the outer `{` the `[^{}]*` run stops at the nested `{` before reaching "drain_id", and from the inner `{` the run ends at `}` before "drain_id". The repo's own fixture in test/g15-drain-failure-visible.test.ts:54 confirms `ticksByLabel: { tick: 1 }` is present in the summary. Result: `_drain_summary` is always empty, the entry prints "no drain summary (JSON with drain_id) found" and exits 3 on drain attempt 1 on every real run, so termination.state is never read and 判据 9 / Z1 / Z3 can never pass. The correct-by-construction path (line-wise JSON.parse, as scripts/check-drain-failures.mjs does) was not used at the shell boundary.

Same brace-free regex is used to extract the per-round drain reason for the mandated progress line and drain-attempts.jsonl, so on the real summary it yields nothing and the recorded/printed reason degrades to "parse_error" for every attempt — §1.3 requires the real per-round drain reason in both the progress line and the run record.

判别性缺失 for 判据 5 and 6: no test ever executes bin/e0-regression.sh's cross-drain loop. The 判据 5 test re-implements the loop inside the test itself (a local for-loop calling readTerminationFromDrain) and the 判据 6 test likewise; the only entry-level assertions are text greps on the script source (`/while\s*:/`, `/hit drain count limit/`, `/sleep.*DRAIN_BACKOFF/`). Spec §2 判据 5 demands the entry actually run a second drain and exit 0, and 判据 6 demands the entry actually exit non-zero naming the limit hit. Because the entry's own bash-level drain-summary extraction and termination read are never executed by any test, the blocker above passes the suite unnoticed — this is the §0 shape of proving a contract against a fixture rather than the real path.

The driver now hard-depends on an unevidenced store-cli contract: `"$LOOP_ENGINE_RUNNER" "$LOOP_STORE_CLI" "$TRIGGER_STORE_DIR" list open`, and exits 3 ("failed to list open triggers") for any non-zero status. Neither the spec's ground truth nor docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_a9_tick_trigger_01.md evidences a `list` subcommand (only put and `claim open done tick` are recorded as measured). It is satisfied only by a fake runner that returns "[]" for `list` (test/a9-tick-trigger.test.ts:127-137). If the real store-cli has no `list` subcommand or a different output shape, every invocation of bin/deep-research-loop.sh — including the production agent-harness profile path, which is outside this package's §1 scope — fails at exit 3, regressing E0c1 behavior (判据 8).

§1.3 requires each round's runs_root to be appended to the run record; drain-attempts.jsonl records attempt/exit/reason/termination_state/tick_head_seq/elapsed_seconds but never runs_root (it is only incidentally present inside drain-N.stdout.log).

Stale comment: the archival header still says the loop's output lands in run.stdout.log / run.stderr.log, but the loop now writes per-attempt drain-<n>.stdout.log / drain-<n>.stderr.log; no such files are produced any more.
